clue.text: In which the fieldfare, say, may be hampered?

definitions.text: In which the fieldfare, say, may be hampered?

parts.words: In which the fieldfare, say, may be hampered?
parts.note: fieldfare looks like the thrush but is read as fare eaten in a field, and hampered means packed in a hamper

explanation.surface: A bird called a fieldfare finds itself trapped or hindered somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The fieldfare is a bird, but split it as 'field fare': food for an outdoor meal, which is packed in a hamper.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor meal's food is carried in a wicker hamper, the container this phrase names.

clue.text: Quiet finish? Not yet decided!

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet
an ending is a finish

explanation.surface: A peaceful conclusion, but the outcome is still unresolved.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter awaiting a verdict or decision is still undetermined.

clue.text: Composer, drops in, fell

indicators.note: drops means the composer's name loses the following word

parts.note: Chopin was the Polish composer

explanation.surface: A composer drops by and then falls over.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell a tree is to cut it down with an axe.

clue.text: Visitor from Spain, curious to see most unusual nut-tree

definitions.text: Visitor from Spain, curious to see most unusual nut-tree

parts.words: Visitor from Spain, curious to see most unusual nut-tree
parts.note: alludes to the nursery rhyme I Had a Little Nut Tree, in which the King of Spain's daughter comes to visit the tree

explanation.surface: A Spanish tourist travels to see a remarkable tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In the English nursery rhyme 'I had a little nut tree', bearing a silver nutmeg and a golden pear, 'The King of Spain's daughter came to visit me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish king's daughter bears the royal title of princess in Spain.

clue.text: Gangster group carrying equipment

indicators.note: carrying means the word for group holds the word for equipment inside

parts.note: a band is a group
a rig is equipment, as in a drilling rig

explanation.surface: A criminal gang is transporting gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit or outlaw, a robber in a lawless band.

clue.text: Team putting spin on the ball

explanation.definitionFit: A side is a sports squad, and in billiards side is spin put on the cue ball.

clue.text: Demand to support former wife makes one cry out!

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word is placed beneath the other

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
a claim is a demand

explanation.surface: A divorcee's demand for maintenance makes someone shout.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to shout suddenly in surprise or emotion.

clue.text: One who works with counter-intelligence?

parts.note: counter-intelligence suggests spying, but read it as knowledge used behind a shop counter

explanation.surface: An agent employed in espionage.
explanation.definitionFit: A retail worker serves customers across the counter in a store.

clue.text: Possibly the first blunder or main error

indicators.note: error suggests the letters of the preceding words are mistaken and rearranged

explanation.surface: The opening mistake might be a slip or a major mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' signals an anagram of BLUNDER OR MAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: First, second and third are examples of numbers showing position in a sequence.

clue.text: Worker absent to see Rugby play

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
someone off work is absent

explanation.surface: An employee skips work to go and watch a rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a player fends off a tackler with an outstretched arm, a recognised move of the game.

clue.text: One who instigates some Hindu ceremonies

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble around a few religious rites in India.
explanation.definitionFit: To induce something is to bring it about, so an instigator is one who causes events.

clue.text: Irishman's first in residence, settled

indicators.note: in places the Irishman's letter inside the word for residence

parts.note: a pad is slang for a home or flat

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word Irishman's

explanation.surface: An Irish lodger has finally made a home of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that has been settled has been cleared with money handed over.

clue.text: Cronin's doctor does not begin to purfle

indicators.note: does not begin tells us to drop the opening letter of the doctor's name

parts.note: Dr Finlay is the Scottish country doctor in A. J. Cronin's stories, later a British TV series

explanation.surface: A novelist's doctor character refuses to start decorating something.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Finlay, A. J. Cronin's Scottish GP (famous from the British TV series Dr Finlay's Casebook), loses his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Purfling is a decorative edging set into a violin or cabinet, so to purfle is to set ornament into a surface.

clue.text: Try one run over airstrip

parts.note: to try someone's patience is to tax it
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone tries running across a landing strip.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft moves slowly along the ground on its wheels before take-off and after landing.

clue.text: Do but correct such lack of faith

indicators.note: correct tells us to fix the order of the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Fix 'do but' to express a want of belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correct' signals an anagram of DO BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubt is uncertainty or a want of conviction.

clue.text: High mark in examination for brightest star

explanation.definitionFit: An alpha is a top grade for work, and the alpha star is the most luminous in a constellation.

clue.text: Foreign lady soaring over?

indicators.note: over suggests the letters of soaring are turned over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman from abroad is flying high above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the anagram signal for the letters of 'soaring'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian form of address for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs or madam.

clue.text: Cover the wrong way round on novel? What a predicament!

indicators.note: the wrong way round means the word for cover is written backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover for a pot or box
Emma is Jane Austen's novel

explanation.surface: A book jacket has been put on upside down, causing embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way round' reverses the cover; 'novel' is Jane Austen's book, and 'on' just sets one piece against the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation at a tricky choice between two unwelcome options, a quandary.

clue.text: Drinks with bib semi-askew

indicators.note: askew means crooked, so the letters are set out of line and rearranged

explanation.surface: A baby drinks while their bib is half twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'askew' signals an anagram of BIB and SEMI together.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbibing is a formal word for swallowing liquid, especially alcohol.

clue.text: Listen to UK composer

indicators.note: listen to says the answer sounds like the word for the clue's country

parts.note: the UK is Britain

explanation.surface: Hear the work of a British composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Britten was a 20th-century English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten wrote operas such as Peter Grimes.

clue.text: Drink more, perhaps, as overlord?

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word more may appear in a different order

explanation.surface: A ruler asks for another drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals an anagram of MORE, giving REMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is a supreme leader or boss.

clue.text: Whine about this Roman punk hairstyle…

indicators.note: about means the word for whine goes around the Latin word

parts.note: to moan is to complain or whine
hic is Latin for this, the language of the Romans

explanation.surface: Someone complains about an Italian man's spiky haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' looks like a person, but 'this Roman' asks for the Latin word for 'this'; 'about' has the complaint go round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of upright hair down the middle of a shaved head, named after a Native American people.

clue.text: Feeling of unease in men in Kuala Lumpur, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the answer sounds like the people named

parts.note: Kuala Lumpur is the capital of Malaysia, home of the Malays

explanation.surface: Men in the Malaysian capital report feeling uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a vague sense of discomfort or illness.

clue.text: Nothing in ice-cream wafer can be put on the head

definitions.text: can be put on the head

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the word for the ice-cream wafer

parts.note: a cornet is a cone for ice cream
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An empty ice-cream cone could be worn as a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crown worn by nobles is placed on top of someone's head.

clue.text: … hard work to Italian

parts.note: taken as written
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: Labour is given over to an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on from the previous one with an ellipsis; 'Italian' gives IL, the Italian for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Toil means strenuous labour, exhausting effort.

clue.text: W-H-E-A-T?

parts.note: the letters show a cereal word written out one by one, and they also name a kind of that cereal

explanation.definitionFit: Spelt is an ancient grain related to common bread wheat, and the word set out letter by letter has been written that way.

clue.text: Prune garnish?

explanation.definitionFit: To prune a hedge is to cut it back neatly, and decorative edging on clothing or a dish is its adornment.

clue.text: The third man's fruit?

parts.note: the film The Third Man features the character Harry with this citrus surname

explanation.definitionFit: A green citrus fruit, also the surname of Harry, the title character of the film The Third Man.

clue.text: University hospital leaders admit soldiers in this state

indicators.note: admit means the leading letters take the soldiers inside them
leaders asks for the opening letters of University and hospital

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, British reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Senior staff at a university hospital let troops in.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the United States, its capital Salt Lake City.

clue.text: Chemical salt approved after dark, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the answer sounds like the words built from the clue

parts.note: night means dark, and right means approved, coming after it

explanation.surface: A chemical compound gets the nod once night falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'approved' is RIGHT and 'dark' is NIGHT; 'after' puts RIGHT second, and 'we hear' turns NIGHT RIGHT into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound formed from nitrous acid, used for example to cure meats.

clue.text: Decimal point of extreme force

parts.note: decimal counting is done in tens
a point of the compass, here East

explanation.surface: The decimal point is a matter of extreme power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decimal' means counting IN TENS; 'point' is a compass point, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense describes something very strong or severe in degree.

clue.text: Turn one's head, perhaps, to discover where secret is kept

indicators.note: perhaps hints the words before it can appear in another order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving the letters ONES

explanation.surface: Glancing round might reveal where a hidden secret is stored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals an anagram of TURN ONES HEAD; 'Turn' looks like the instruction but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something to yourself is the idiom for a confidence held privately.
